PullRequest.Title: sessions: Customize application badge session categories
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Add one object setting, `sessions.applicationBadge`, to choose which unarchived sessions contribute to the application badge when `sessions.showApplicationBadge` is enabled:

```json
"sessions.applicationBadge": {
  "inputNeeded": true,
  "unread": false,
  "ciFailing": false
}
```

- Keep the existing badge enablement setting and its product-quality default.
- Default the badge to input-needed sessions only; unread sessions and CI failures are opt-in.
- Apply option changes immediately and count each matching session only once.
- Reuse the existing failing-CI eligibility rules, including Agent Merge handling, and avoid subscribing to CI state when that option is disabled.
- Document the options and cross-link the settings in their localized descriptions.

## Validation

- Passed targeted ESLint for all three changed files.
- Passed the repository formatter verification and `git diff --check`.
- Added regression coverage for all eight option combinations, default values, deduplication, archived/in-progress exclusions, live configuration updates/reset, and badge enablement/clearing.
- Compile, full hygiene, and focused unit tests could not run: dependency restoration encountered registry `ENOTCONN` failures and Foundry native-download failures (`ENOTCONN`/HTTP 401). Installing JavaScript dependencies without lifecycle scripts enabled the standalone lint/format checks, but build dependencies remained unavailable.

Focused tests to run once dependencies are available:

```sh
./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/electron-browser/sessionsApplicationBadge.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/blockedSessions/test/browser/blockedSessions.test.ts
```

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench restoration with the badge enabled and default options
Scenarios.CriticalPath: At WorkbenchPhase.AfterRestored, the contribution synchronously reads configuration and performs one O(N) scan. If the resulting count is positive it renders the existing fixed-size Windows icon and dispatches the existing native-host badge call; GitHub work is not observed by the new default because ciFailing is false.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: INativeHostService.setApplicationBadge sends the count and, on Windows, a fixed-size PNG data URL to the main process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one call on initial observation when the count is positive; zero-count startup is suppressed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same badge IPC and Windows canvas serialization occurred before the diff; the default category change generally reduces the sessions contributing to it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The fixed-size icon generation occurs synchronously before IPC on Windows; the Promise returned by IPC is not awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N deduplicated sessions returned by ISessionsManagementService.getSessions(); only unarchived sessions are counted.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The badge computation is synchronous and single-threaded. The native-host call is asynchronous and not awaited. Existing GitHub session polling runs independently and is not added or rescheduled by this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The default input-needed path does not observe failingCISessions, so its lazy PR/CI model references are not acquired. Session lists are recomputed by the existing management service; no new cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the contribution phase, lazy observable dependencies, O(N) scan, and native-host call path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The repository does not establish a hard upper bound for N, but the changed default removes unread/CI observation and does not add startup work relative to the old all-category badge.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Default startup performs less reactive CI work than before, while retaining the existing bounded scan and badge IPC.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opting into CI-failing sessions and reacting to PR/CI changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Badge recomputation reads already-reactive PR and CI model state and scans N sessions. It does not await network. A native badge update occurs only when the derived numeric count changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing polling refreshes PR details and reviews, CI check runs, and review threads for eligible PRs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Effectively per unique PR/head after shared model and in-flight refresh coalescing, on the existing polling cadence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The polling contribution already acquired, refreshed, and polled these models for sessions before this diff. The old badge also observed blocked-session PR/CI state when enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous and off the badge computation's critical path; the badge reacts when cached observable state changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update the application badge after the distinct matching-session count changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC per distinct emitted count; derived number equality suppresses unchanged-count downstream runs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old badge used the same renderer and native-host call on blocked/unread count changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Windows performs fixed-size canvas drawing and PNG serialization synchronously, then dispatches IPC without awaiting it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N sessions, reduced by archive/in-progress/PR eligibility; model instances and network refreshes are keyed by U unique owner/repo/PR/head combinations after ReferenceCollection sharing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The pre-existing GitHubPullRequestPollingContribution starts per-session pollers, but ReferenceCollection shares models by PR/head and model refresh promises coalesce concurrent refreshes. No new concurrency limiter or burst is introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: PR models are shared by owner/repo/PR and CI models by owner/repo/PR/head. delayedStore acquires replacement references before releasing old ones, preventing model teardown on recomputation. Cold models begin neutral/undefined and are populated by the existing polling contribution; warm models are reused.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: model keys, reference sharing, delayed-store lifecycle, refresh coalescing, and polling call paths were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneous sessions and unique PRs is not bounded in the reviewed code. Enabling CI can add lightweight references for needs-input sessions, but the underlying model and network lifecycle is already owned by the existing poller.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new projection is lazy, shares existing models, adds no network boundary, and replaces the old blocked-session observation rather than stacking another production observer.

Scenarios.Scenario: Changing badge category settings at runtime
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The configuration observable invalidates the derived count immediately. The synchronous work is one session scan plus optional fixed-size Windows icon rendering; any native-host IPC is dispatched without awaiting it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send a new badge or clear the badge when the selected categories change the count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one call for a settings change that changes the numeric count; no call for a stable zero and unchanged derived counts do not propagate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no category-setting event before the diff, so only the existing global enablement and session-state changes could trigger this boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fixed-size Windows image generation is synchronous; IPC itself is asynchronous and unawaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One user configuration event triggers a scan over N sessions; enabling CI considers U shared PR/head model keys.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Configuration events are handled serially in the renderer. Existing model acquisition is synchronous and reference-counted; existing network pollers continue independently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Disabling CI stops observing failingCISessions and releases its delayed-store references. Re-enabling reuses models retained by the existing polling contribution; there is no retained option-history cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the configuration observable and derived equality behavior are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Interactive option edits are infrequent; exact N is unknown, but work is linear and no request fan-out is caused by the setting event.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This is intentional, bounded work directly required to apply an infrequent user setting immediately.

Scenarios.Scenario: Existing blocked-session indicators and lists after the CI eligibility helper refactor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing consumers continue to read blockedSessions or blockedSessionsWithReasons. The new failingCISessions derived is lazy and is not observed by those consumers, so it does not add a second pass there.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read shared PR and CI model state whose refresh/polling is owned by the existing GitHub polling contribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Model reads scale with eligible sessions, but network refresh cardinality remains per shared unique PR/head and is not initiated here.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same helper body was inline in _getBlockedSession and consumed the same shared model state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No network is awaited or started by this helper; it consumes cached observables.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N sessions and B blocked sessions; existing blockedSessionsWithReasons performs its prior O(N) eligibility pass and sorts B results.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new asynchronous work or boundary concurrency is introduced for existing consumers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing structural equality for blocked session arrays remains intact. Shared PR/CI references retain their delayed-store rollover semantics. The new derived releases references when its last observer is removed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all production constructors and observable reads of BlockedSessions were searched and traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Existing UI consumers and session counts vary, but no production caller observes both projections on one BlockedSessions instance in the traced code.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The extraction preserves the existing hot path, and the additional projection activates only for the new badge CI option.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and traced startup, configuration changes, live session updates, native badge IPC/rendering, and shared GitHub PR/CI model polling. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression was found; no findings were submitted.
